Subject: Post-call synthesis: model slate + benchmark links + latency runbook

Thanks again for the time today, Anika — quick synthesis and concrete next steps so we keep momentum. I captured the recommended model slate based on the discovery (high-throughput customer messaging + summary accuracy requirement):

Recommended model slate (initial pilot):
- redwood-open-7B-q4f32 (best balance: 1.8k TPS projected, strong ROUGE/F1 on your sample prompts)
- redwood-mix-13B-8bit (higher quality; ~850 TPS; lower hallucination on clinical snippets)
- fallback: redwood-open-3B (cheap, ~3k TPS for basic routing/async tasks)

Redwood-verified performance snapshot (on g4dn-like instance, measured with our profiler):
- redwood-open-7B-q4f32: sustained TPS (tokens/sec): 1,800; latency p50: 22 ms; p95: 48 ms; p99: 110 ms
- redwood-mix-13B-8bit: TPS: 850; p50: 38 ms; p95: 95 ms; p99: 220 ms
- redwood-open-3B: TPS: 3,100; p50: 12 ms; p95: 28 ms; p99: 60 ms

What I attached/linked:
- redwood_verified_profiles.csv — full performance profile and kernel selection notes per model (attached)
- medframe_benchmark_trace.jsonl — a small trace from the synthetic workload that matches your burst pattern (attached)
- prompt_set_v1.txt — 40 representative prompts we used for quality evaluation (attached)
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1q2w3e-redwood-medframe-benchmarks

Quality/regression guardrails we recommend for the pilot:
- Keep a held-out prompt set (we provided prompt_set_v1.txt). Run nightly regression checks on a small sample (5–10 prompts) and alert on >5% drop in QA metrics (ROUGE/F1 or domain-specific metric).
- Canary route: start 10% traffic to redwood-mix-13B-8bit for the first week, measure divergence vs. 7B baseline.
- KV prefix caching for repeated patient-context queries — recommended TTL 2h for chat flows to keep cold-start tokens low.

Mutual action plan (first pass):
1) Redwood: provide full benchmark artifacts and runbook by EOD Friday — (Dylan) — actioned, attached.
2) MedFrame: share 1 sample anonymized conversation batch for accuracy checks — (Anika) — aim: Tue 6/23.
3) Redwood infra/solutions call to scope Dedicated vs Hosted latency tradeoffs — (Karthik + MedFrame infra) — schedule next week.
4) Procurement: provide PO template or timing constraints — (MedFrame Procurement) — target: decision by end of July.

Please let me know if the p99 numbers look off relative to your expectation; I called out p99 because we know your SLA target is under 250 ms for interactive flows (we’re comfortably under that for the 13B in our tests; 7B is much lower).

Thanks — attaching the CSV and traces. Happy to jump back on a quick 20-min readout with engineering to walk traces.

—

Hi Anika — quick technical follow-up to answer your points: 

1) p99 measurement details: the p99=220 ms for redwood-mix-13B-8bit was measured with:
   - avg context: ~2.1 KB (≈ 450 tokens)
   - synthetic KV-cache miss ratio: 20% (we inject cold-starts to reflect first-turn queries)
   - batch size: adaptive batching to keep latency SLO at 200 ms for p95; p99 includes tail from occasional GPU context switch and small queueing spikes.

2) Quantization / RAM footprint: attached is a short table in redwood_verified_profiles.csv but quick numbers:
   - redwood-mix-13B-8bit: ~40 GB GPU memory (with activation checkpointing off); with activation checkpointing on and 8-bit quantization we see ~28–32 GB usable.
   - redwood-open-7B-q4f32: ~18–20 GB nominal.

3) Prompt mapping: the clinical summarization prompts are labeled in prompt_set_v1.txt under header "CLIN_SUM_01..12" — those are the ones we used for the QA metrics. We can produce a compliance export (anonymized) if needed.

4) Traces: I pulled two representative traces from the bench run and left them in medframe_benchmark_trace.jsonl (see the drive link). They include token-level timings and kernel selection flags if you want to look at where the tail comes from.

If it helps, I can join a short call with your infra folks and run the trace live through our profiler so you can see p95/p99 buckets in real time.

—Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
